messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pagerduty alert: GPU queue growth detected in `us-west-2` cluster -> high pending pods, autoscaler failing to add nodes. Incident channel created. Root cause suspected: nodegroup launch template drift + attach role failures.
Ava (oncall): I'm on it. checking cluster state now.
Ava (oncall): kubectl get pods -n inference | grep Pending | wc -l -> 312 pending, many Pending due to "node(s) didn't match pod affinity/taint" and Insufficient GPUs.
Miguel (infra): :eyes: I'm pulling autoscaler logs, might be hitting ASG scale limits or IAM attachrole failures. Can you paste an example pending pod?
Ava (oncall): pasted one: `Events: Normal Scheduled 2m default-scheduler Successfully assigned inference/worker-abc to ip-10-0-45-128.us-west-2.compute.internal` then `Warning FailedAttachVolume 1m kubelet attach/detach failed for volume...` and `Warning FailedScheduling 30s  kubelet 0/12 nodes are available: Insufficient gpu, node(s) had taint that the pod didn't tolerate.`
Priya (sre): Autoscaler logs show repeated scale-up attempts but instances never become Ready. Here's snippet from cluster-autoscaler: ```I0404 17:42:11 scale_up.go:343] Best option: ip-10-0-50-0.us-west-2 1 nodes, predicted 0 pods remain unschedulable
I0404 17:43:13 event.go:210] Failed to attach IAM role to instance profile: error attaching iam role: AccessDenied: AttachRolePolicy```
Jared (ml-infra): That `AccessDenied` smells like the nodegroup's launch template is referencing an instance profile that no longer exists or the IAM role condition was tightened. We recently rolled a launchtemplate for newer AMI two days ago — could be drift.
Sam (eng): Customer Success says a few customers reported model requests timing out. CS: "we're seeing 500s for batch inference jobs started ~17:40 UTC". Impact looks moderate-high.
Customer Success: We're triaging customer-impacted orgs and will escalate to AE if SLA breach likely.
Ava (oncall): Quick mitigation: scaling down non-critical training job DaemonSet, evicting best-effort pods from GPU nodes to free slots for inference. Executing `kubectl delete pod -l job=training --namespace=ml-workloads --grace-period=0 --force`.
Priya (sre): Good. Also marking this as P1. I'm going to set an autoscaler max increase override to allow burst: `kubectl annotate deployment cluster-autoscaler rpa/burst=true` (conceptual) — actually we'll patch the autoscaler configmap to temporarily raise `maxNodeProvisionTime` and `scaleUpLimit` to allow faster grow.
Miguel (infra): I'm verifying ASG limits: `aws autoscaling describe-auto-scaling-groups --auto-scaling-group-names gpu-asg-usw2-prod` -> MaxSize is 12, Desired 12, Instances 12. There are no more capacity to request. We need to request an increase or create a new nodegroup.
Jared (ml-infra): If ASG at max, CA will keep queuing scale attempts but nothing will launch. Two options: 1) bump ASG max and trigger provision, 2) create fallback nodegroup (smaller instances with multiple GPUs) with a compatible launch template and attachrole.
Ava (oncall): Can we hotfix by adding an ondemand nodegroup manually? I can approve if infra ok.
Miguel (infra): I can create a temporary nodegroup, but we need to ensure Launch Template has the correct instance profile/attach role. Last LT update introduced `iam:PassRole` condition that blocks the autoscaler-assumed role. I'll create a LT clone with the older instance-profile and no restrictive condition.
Sam (eng): If we create a new nodegroup, CA might still prefer existing groups. We should label it `node.kubernetes.io/instance-type=gpu-fallback` and annotate for autoscaler. Also ensure taint policy matches pods tolerations.
Priya (sre): While Miguel works on nodegroup, we'll enable fallback routing at the serving layer: route low-priority inference to `cpu-pool` with degraded perf to keep requests returning instead of timing out. Jared, can you flip routing?
Jared (ml-infra): Routing patched: `service-configs/production -> route: allow-degraded: true` deployed. Telemetry shows error rate on inference down from 8% -> 3% for affected customers.
incident-bot: Audit note: escalation path triggered — paging oncall, infra, and sre.
pagerduty-bot: Acknowledge: incident acknowledged by Ava (oncall).
Miguel (infra): Creating fallback nodegroup now. Command: ```eksctl create nodegroup --cluster=prod-usw2 --name=gpu-fallback-1 --node-type=p4d.8xlarge --nodes=2 --node-ami=custom-gpu-ami-2026 --instance-profile=prod-gpu-node-profile-v2```
Miguel (infra): Launch template clone in progress. Warning: `AttachRolePolicy` check failing in dry-run due to missing `iam:PassRole` permission for eksctl user. I'll temporarily use infra deploy role to attach.
Ava (oncall): ETA?
Miguel (infra): ~8-12 minutes to spin and join nodes, assuming no EC2 capacity issues.
Priya (sre): Meanwhile, let's avoid further churn on existing nodegroups — don't re-run launchtemplate updates until we confirm fix. Add a note to the deployment runbook.
Sam (eng): Heads-up: customers on `org-42` still hitting 500s. CS please share list for timeline.
Customer Success: Shared org list in DM. We notified them of a degraded performance alert and that we are provisioning fallback capacity.
Jared (ml-infra): New nodes starting to join: `kubectl get nodes | grep gpu-fallback` -> `ip-10-0-66-77 Ready` and `ip-10-0-66-78 NotReady` (joining kubelet). Pod scheduling happening onto new node.
Ava (oncall): I'm seeing pods transition: `kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep Pending` dropping from 312 -> 45. Good.
Priya (sre): Confirmed autoscaler resume: CA detecting new nodegroup, removing some scale-up attempts. Will watch for any AttachRole errors in the node bootstrap logs.
Miguel (infra): Postmortem note: we traced root cause to a recent LT change that added a restrictive IAM condition (on `iam:PassRole`) which prevented the instance profile attach during autoscaling. Manual nodegroup creation succeeded because infra deploy role has broader permissions.
Sam (eng): For immediate mitigation, recommend: 1) revert LT change or relax IAM condition, 2) add a secondary nodegroup as permanent buffer, 3) improve CA metrics/alerts for ASG MaxSize hit.
Ava (oncall): Customer impact: brief period (17:40–17:58 UTC) of degraded inference for some orgs, rate-limited by queue and timeouts. CS drafting post-incident note.
Customer Success: We're prepping a customer-facing timeline and will include mitigations and ETA for full resolution.
Jared (ml-infra): Observability: token cost/latency graphs show tail latency spike correlating to queue growth. Back to baseline after fallback nodes ready.
Priya (sre): Next steps: schedule follow-up postmortem, assign owners: Miguel -> LT/IAM fix and LT rollback; Jared -> restore autoscaler config; Sam -> routing docs for degraded modes; Ava -> customer comms.
Miguel (infra): Will open PR to revert LT and submit IAM policy change request for approval.
Ava (oncall): Closing active pager for now. Monitoring for 1 hour before declaring resolved. tagging this thread P1 -> mitigation in place. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Incident state updated: Mitigated. Root cause suspected: launch template IAM condition preventing autoscaler-managed role from attaching instance profile, causing ASG at max and nodes not becoming Ready.
Priya (sre): Recording timeline and linking runbook snippets. Will schedule retrospective meeting.
Ava (oncall): Thanks team. If anyone sees a regression ping here. :thumbsup:
